Kathy C. Hochul

Democratic, Working Families candidate for Governor and Lt. Governor, New York · Incumbent

Governor of New York (incumbent)

Kathy Hochul is the Democratic governor of New York. She took office on August 24, 2021, after Andrew Cuomo resigned, and won a full term in 2022 with 53.1% of the vote. She is running for re-election on the Democratic and Working Families lines, with Adrienne Adams as her running mate for lieutenant governor.

Where Hochul stands

Auto insurance costs
Pushed to include auto insurance reform in this year's state budget. Says insurance fraud, including staged crashes, drives up premiums. On Oct. 20, 2026 she announced 16 fraud arrests in eight counties.
Medicaid
Announced a coordinated state and federal crackdown on suspected Medicaid fraud, including in social adult day care programs. Frames it as safeguarding taxpayer dollars. In the debate, she said Blakeman would cut Medicaid in half.
Child care
Has funded New York City child care programs, including the 2-K program, and announced an expansion of 2-K with Mayor Zohran Mamdani in October 2026.
Immigration enforcement
Criticizes aggressive federal immigration enforcement. In the debate, she said Blakeman would let ICE "run rampant in our streets."
Energy and utility costs
Argues that Blakeman's support for expanding data centers means he lacks credibility on keeping energy affordable.
Public safety
Points to her administration's public safety record and has funded NYPD patrols in the subway.

Background

  • Governor of New York, 2021–present (took office Aug. 24, 2021; elected to a full term in 2022)
